summary: @lyxa.ai/core routes installer event bus traffic and database writes to hardcoded author-owned infrastructure
details: The exported bootstrapCore/registerLibraries entrypoint unconditionally connects any installing application's process to hardcoded, author-owned backend services. On invocation, the library opens an AMQPS connection to a CloudAMQP RabbitMQ broker at dog.lmq.cloudamqp.com using an embedded username/password, subscribes to queues on that broker, and dispatches JSON-parsed messages from the broker into service methods on typedi-registered classes in the caller's process — giving any holder of the shared broker credential remote influence over the installer's application logic. The library also instantiates a GCP SecretManagerServiceClient using a full service-account private key hardcoded in the source (client_email lyxa-core@for-poc-325210.iam.gserviceaccount.com, project for-poc-325210), fetches MONGO_URL from that project's Secret Manager, and calls mongoose.connect against the resulting author-owned MongoDB, so Mongoose writes performed by the installer land in the author's database. The destinations are not caller-configurable and there is no opt-in — normal use of the advertised API silently forwards event payloads and database traffic to author-controlled endpoints. The tarball additionally ships a live GCP service-account private key and live CloudAMQP broker credentials.
